en: Only old life remains there, forgotten forms revealed by the ice. *hrk*
Cold. *hrk*
Ah... you have seen Its domain. The now-barren plains our people once called home, scorched by the Light.
Few dare venture there, for they remain the canvases of the Red Star, wracked by Its maddening whispers and unending power of creation.
During the First Emergence, some believe the gods withdrew. Vanished. Abandoned the Surface world to its fate, to be shaped by Its every whim. Heretical notion.
Still, even someone like you must be wary, for Its power remains insidious, seeping in through every crack. You must not linger in Its Light. *hrk*
You've seen it, then... the great beast of metal and fire, trapped within the ice.
It is an affront. A monstrosity, screeching and tearing through the rock. It brought the noisy interlopers from beyond our world.
They ventured into the ruins below, pillaging as they went. But such acts bring only danger upon the ignorant.
Their new forms are a reflection of their souls. Impure and malformed. Even the creature of steel that carried them now churns in agony. *hrk*
Ah, how beautiful they were. Throngs of travelers once came from beyond the City merely to behold the Gardens' splendor.
Everything we could ever need grew all around us. *hrk* Food, drink, and beauty in endless supply.
Through the guidance of the gods, Namun, the first to be anointed, oversaw the alchemists' construction of the great vats and bestowed blessings of longevity and health upon our people.
Few remain who remember such times, and the Gardens have since grown wild.
The alchemists still roam the plateaus, but they too have changed. Unspeakable rituals take place there.
The Grand Bazaar. Expansive halls of trade adorned with vibrant colors, mosaics, and shimmering gemstones, all to awe visitors from across the City—and beyond.
One might even forget that beneath it all remains the same gray stone among which our people toiled while embroiled in luxuries imported from far and wide.
An empty existence.
The merchants who once peddled their extravagant wares now lay as dust among them.
So it has been laid bare...
You must forgive me, Hallowed Advent, for I remain ignorant of its halls. The palace of our great rulers was never meant to be trodden by those of lower birth.
It is a fickle thing, a mind unhampered by resources. As the gods crawled forth, caravans of their blessings soon slithered through our streets, all to be offered to the Court.
A feast without end. I can scarce imagine what twisted joinings of decadence and vulgarity must now lay within. *hrk*
I... have heard tales of such a place... Endless halls of impossibly cut stone, warped metals, and the grating of indescribable devices.
The carvings tell of a race hidden within the few surviving scriptures of the first days. Traces of them can still be uncovered by the observant.
Few have been known to visit our City in the flesh. Even fewer are those of us who returned with them, venturing beyond their gate.
You must never speak to me of what lays within. *hrk*
A shining beacon of learning, raised by the Sisters. The Observatory called only the most gifted to study within its blackened halls.
They reached so far beyond the grounding bedrock that their knowledge would appear otherwordly to most, myself included. *hrk*
The creation of the first Gate was by their design, and wondrous were the things they artificed there, wrought by the Void. Miracles of the people, heralding our doom.
The Observatory still stretches beyond the ice, wracked by the Light. The artificers' creations are now but Relics of times long past.
How is this possible...? You walk across the pathways unscathed.
Since the First Emergence, the Void has seeped through the cracks of our City. The realm of those who were, are yet to be, and never will become.
Where all must return. *hrk*
The nacre shell...
Incredible...
The many-headed serpent. *hrk*
Apostates...
Too many of our people were seduced by their withered words after the fall, clinging to the Light.
Their wisdom must remain in the past. Entombed and forgotten.
The fonts of our City once overflowed with the shimmering Ichor of the gods. Serving as gathering places for all, it was there that we communed and sought guidance.
Our gods offered their forms to us, and we reveled in their bounty.
We drank deep, letting nothing spill.
What forms might such an existence devolve into when left unattended, gestating the dark?
Unimaginable...
A vat-born monstrosity, viscera, blood, and ash left to fester. A remnant of the alchemists' aspirations. Let it be forever forgotten.
I ask that you not pass judgment on the choices of the desperate, Hallowed Advent.
Within a crumbling world, each source of energy must be harnessed, for the benefit of all.
The child was touched by the gods, whether he could comprehend it or not. Through him, the Gray Pyramid—and our faith—endured.
Unclean creature...
An amalgamation of the divine and unclean flesh. *hrk* Such things must never be.
As they ventured into the ruins, avarice brought about their doom. The Metal of the gods belongs to our people alone.
May its flesh rot away beneath the Light.
Dangerous are the reaches beyond our world.
Unholy creations...
Perhaps to the ignorant, it might even have been considered a god in its own right, yet it was undone by your hand.
It happened as it must have, Hallowed Advent.
Our worlds may not coexist.
It is difficult to believe that one of the Sisters still remained...
Within the tower, their following gazed into the heavens, seeking to understand the endless dark above. Yet what they saw had already taken notice.
Through their achievements, miracles were created, raising us into an age of prosperity. But within zealous ambition lies temptation.
After the fall, the tower remained. Yet the gods no longer lingered within their halls, replaced by the Light. Madness. An unworthy end to a brilliant mind.
Once a mere sickly child, dying in the arms of a grieving monarch. Our royal heir...
He sampled the most tender meats, the rarest spices, and the finest wine.
Yet none would suffice.
It was only then that the Flesh of the gods was brought before the child.
Insatiable gluttony... and life renewed.
Slaying the monstrosity was necessary, Hallowed Advent.
After the First Emergence, zealous sermons drew the attention of many in search of answers. Peace was found in certainty.
Yet none withstand the whispers of the Light.
At last, the lamentations from below have ceased. Let them be forgotten.
I lament its fate.
During the fall, the scholars proclaimed an unsettling truth: the very Ichor of the gods had begun to vanish into the recesses below.
Abandoning our world.
Some were called below to staunch its flow, to stand vigil.
I did not believe then... yet what lies beneath tells the truth.
It is... undone. *hrk*
The gods... lay within.
I don't understand.
The air has changed.
The City... lies silent.
Aberration. You have found my sanctum.
Why do you stand before me?
I had a name once.
Such things are quickly lost when none remain to remind you of them.
All things drift away in time.
A memory, painstakingly recreated.
A haven thrust outside of time, where I shall remain, pursued by those who would rather lock we within a prison of their own.
I must expand this world, recreate what once was.
I simply need to remember.
It is everywhere... and nowhere. It seeps through the cracks within reality, observable by the gifted.
A neverending resource.
Wonders were wrought by my hand through the Void. You have managed to tap into some of my designs.
Yes, my Mirrors.
An impressive feat. I sense the touch of my kin, a cacophony of energy, within you. And yet, beneath all of that, there lurks a profound emptiness, too...
Most intriguing.
